headline: Transport and flow-matching models predict single-cell responses to perturbation
label: Single Cell Perturbation Modeling
summary: Recent preprints apply flow matching and Schrödinger Bridge transport to predict single-cell perturbation responses in learned latent spaces.
synthesis: The common thread is predicting single-cell perturbation responses as transport between control and perturbed states in learned latent spaces. DRIFT separates invariant from perturbation-responsive latent blocks and applies conditional flow matching to the responsive block. scEGFlow uses energy-guided conditional flow matching from control to perturbed states and targets generalization to unseen conditions. PerturbBridge models responses as conditional latent Schrödinger Bridge transport using beta-TCVAE latents with MMD regularization. SHERLOCK treats perturbation effects as latent interventions for causal and combinatorial inference, while Pop-Corn predicts shifts in cell-type composition directly from Perturb-seq data. What is new is the convergence of transport-based formulations on perturbation prediction rather than a single unifying framework. Adjacent work applies optimal transport to integration and spatial modeling, including AtlasOT, MoTRUST, and NexuST, which share the mathematical toolkit but address different problems.
